name: Neo-kitsch
overall: Better than on 2026-11-13, and the biggest single miss of that review is gone: ENTER / LOGIN now reads as firm dark lettering on a rounded bar, and the dashboard EMAIL panel's body is legible. The login input fill, the mailbox header baseline and the BASKET clipping are fixed too. The generated wood is a real step up on the selected store card, which now looks like veneer with the reference's Bonus streak; on the smaller surfaces (mail row, SMG button, BASKET lower band) it is still near-straight, low-contrast lines with none of the reference's lens-shaped figure, and on the dashboard panel and EMAIL card it shows texture artefacts (a hard rectangular patch edge in the panel's lower right, a hard-cut horizontal band across the card). What now gives it away most, flipping between the two: (1) the palette of light text is a pale cream (#E7C686 at peak) where the reference prints a saturated amber (#FFCD79) with a soft halo -- logotype, PRASE labels, clock, header labels; (2) ink on the selected mail row and the SMG button is still grey and pale, now also faintly doubled by the print overlay; (3) the overlay's ghost copies sometimes read as detached hard-edged slivers (the right end of each ENTER bar, the left end of selected surfaces) instead of the reference's soft glow. The reference has a warm bloom around every bright element; ours has ghost copies but no bloom, so it reads cooler and crisper overall. Scores are one reviewer's opinion from 1600-pixel images.
regressions: Print overlay, ENTER / LOGIN bars: the outward copy lands as a separate thin bright sliver just right of each bar's right end, with a dark gap between, so the bar looks like it has a detached strip. The reference has a soft amber halo there, not a second edge. Same effect, milder, at the left end of the selected mail row, the SMG button and the BASKET panel.

Print overlay, header T labels (mailbox and dashboard): the ghost copies of T2/T3/T4 and LEVEL offset right are visibly stronger than the reference's faint ones; at 2.5x they read as a second set of numerals.

Print overlay, selected mail row: the dark text gets a faint doubled copy, which makes the already-pale 'Urgent information (!)' and 'FROM: MOM' look blurred as well as pale. Ink darkness itself is unchanged since 11-13 (darkest pixel 90 in both goldens, reference 57).

Generated veneer, dashboard EMAIL panel: a hard vertical/rectangular edge at the right of the lower-third figure (about x 1350-1360, y 590-620 at 1600x900) where the line pattern stops abruptly. The panel's grain is also soft and low-contrast compared with the reference's crisp, distinct dark lines at native scale.

Generated veneer, EMAIL cascade card: the seam is a hard-edged horizontal band (sharp top and bottom cuts) rather than lines pinching into a point; at full view it reads as a pasted stripe. It is still closer to the reference than the old straight stripes, so this is a new defect, not a net regression.

Not regressions, checked: the darker ink on the ENTER bars is slightly darker than the reference (darkest 70 vs 86) but reads right; the rounded ENTER bar matches (radius a touch smaller than the reference's); the harder right edge of the blue ground matches the reference's rim and removed the old teal cast.

screens.name: Login
screens.verdict: The ENTER / LOGIN bars and the input fields are now right, which fixes what read wrong at a glance; what is left is palette and material: pale cream text where the reference is amber with glow, and a wire band that is uniformly bright.
matches: Layout unchanged and still near-exact: logotype and info box, clock block, both PRASE fields, A/B badges, bottom wire band and disclaimer line.
ENTER / LOGIN: firm dark wide lettering at the reference's size, rounded right corners, chamfered left; the bar no longer vanishes.
Input fields are now the reference's warm maroon-brown.
Violet-to-blue ground now ends in the reference's darker right rim; the old teal cast in the top-right is gone.
The print overlay gives the logotype and info box ghost copies like the reference's.

gaps.text: Light text is pale cream (#E7C686) where the reference is saturated amber (#FFCD79) with a soft halo: logotype, PRASE_6054012, 10:10 PM, NIGHT CITY / AREA. Most noticeable in the logotype and clock.

Bottom wire band: ours is evenly bright pale yellow on every strand; the reference grades from dark orange-brown on the upper plateau strands to bright where the strands bunch on the S-bends, with a warm haze. Ours reads as a solid gold slab in the centre.

ENTER / LOGIN bar: flat fill with no grain and almost no halo, and the print overlay's copy sits as a detached sliver beyond the right end. The reference bar is grainy with a soft glow all round. Label is set 'ENTER / LOGIN' with spaced slash; the reference's slash is tight ('ENTER/ LOGIN') and its face is wider with thinner strokes.
Fine print beside the A/B badges and the bottom disclaimer: ours thinner, dimmer and squarer; the reference's is a brighter, bolder rounded face.
Small type under the logotype and in the info box is a squarer pixel-like face; '57ASD4AV15AA' still reads as '57AGD4AV16AA'.
Logotype ghost copies are offset up-left (radial from centre); the reference's lie to the left at the same height.

since_2026_11_13.text: ENTER / LOGIN bars: label thin, very pale and letter-spaced across the whole bar.
Input fields: duller, greyer brown than the reference's warm maroon-brown.
ENTER / LOGIN bars: square-cut right end where the reference is slightly rounded.
Violet glow spreads further right with a teal cast in the top-right corner.
Small type under the logotype uses a squarer pixel-like face; S reads like 6 or G; stair-stepped logotype edges.

screens.name: Mailbox
screens.verdict: List, body, buttons and header still line up and the header baseline is fixed, but the selected row -- the screen's one gold surface -- still has pale grey text and plain straight grain, and the overlay now blurs that text.
matches: Seven mail rows, envelopes, underlines and tabs at the reference positions; message body matches in font, size, breaks and hyphenation.
Header: SECURITY LEVEL, LEVEL/T1-T4 now share one baseline with the T2 badge, as in the reference.
Four RIFLES buttons match in size, spacing, corner cut and label.
The scallops along the selected row's top edge are gone; the row now has line grain and a seam near FROM: MOM.
Ghost copies on the header and badges are present, as in the reference.

gaps.text: Selected row text 'Urgent information (!)', 'FROM: MOM' and the envelope are pale grey (darkest ~90) where the reference is firm dark brown (~57); the overlay's faint doubled copy makes them look soft as well.

Selected row veneer: ours is near-straight, low-contrast horizontal lines with a faint V seam. The reference has clear dark lines forming lens/eye figures at both ends, a dark seam crease, and darker bevel shading along the bottom edge.
Selected row right end is a hard chamfer with sharp corners; the reference's is rounded.
The tab under the selected row is a black trapezoid with a gold rim, reading as a dark notch; in the reference it is a gold tab only slightly darker than the row.

Header light text (CUSTOMER, LEVEL, SECURITY LEVEL, T1-T4) is pale cream and lighter-weight than the reference's amber; T numerals narrower and taller than the reference's wide square ones; their ghost copies stronger than the reference's.
C/D fine print dimmer than the reference's.

since_2026_11_13.text: Selected row: flat regular wavy stripes, no figured grain, seam, bevelled rim or rounded right end; scallops along the top edge.
Top-right header: SECURITY LEVEL and LEVEL/T1, T3, T4 sit ~8px higher than LEVEL/T2.
T1-T4 numerals narrower and heavier than the reference's wider, squarer letters.
Selected row text a little paler than the reference's dark brown.

screens.name: Store
screens.verdict: The selected card is now convincing -- legible dark ink on a veneer with the reference's Bonus streak -- and BASKET no longer clips; the lighter nav and customer type and the flat small wood surfaces are what remain.
matches: Structure, card geometry, stepped tops, echo stacks, stat grids, socket cells and weapon art all still match closely.
Selected card: numbers, Recoil/Spread/Range and Bonus lines in firm dark ink close to the reference's weight.
Selected card veneer: wavy figured grain with a dark horizontal streak through Bonus, as in the reference; the best wood in the set.
BASKET fine print now fits inside the panel at the reference's size.
Ghost copies on the nav buttons and labels resemble the reference's leftward ones.

gaps.text: Nav labels (RIFLES..PISTOL) and the customer/discount block are lighter in weight and paler than the reference's medium-weight amber; SMG's label is grey (darkest ~66 vs ~50).
SMG button veneer: straight horizontal lines with a seam; the reference has curved figure swirling at both ends and a gold tab with a dark rim at the bottom right (ours is a plain pale patch).

BASKET lower band: almost no visible grain, only a faint seam; the reference has strong figured grain with swirls and a seam, and a darker rim. The panel is also a little more peach than the reference.

Selected card: the upper sweep under the stat numbers is as strong as the Bonus streak and runs straight across; the reference's is weaker and strongest at the right, and has vertical banding in the lower right we do not have. Body text still starts ~10px left of the reference.
MAGNUM 650 HAND GUN still centred ~10px left of the reference on every card; HAND GUN lighter.
No warm bloom around the cards and nav as in the reference; the outlines read crisper.

since_2026_11_13.text: Selected centre card body text thin and pale, starting ~10px further left.
Selected centre card veneer pale and even, one faint line, no figured streak.
BASKET fine print too large and clipped; panel a flat fill with no grain or seam.
MAGNUM 650 HAND GUN ~10px left; HAND GUN lighter and wider-spaced.
Card outer echo strokes crisper and more uniform than the reference's graded stack.

screens.name: Dashboard
screens.verdict: The EMAIL panel body now reads, which was the screen's biggest miss; the two wood surfaces have gained figure but show texture artefacts, and the header labels are dim.
matches: Six cascade cards, staggered placement, chamfers, echo lines and label tabs match.
EMAIL panel body: dark legible text at about the reference's weight.
EMAIL cascade card: vertical grain gathering into a seam with a dark point at the right edge, and a dark rim.
Panel veneer: vertical grain above, a curved figure and crease in the lower third, as in the reference.
Header A/B notes now sit where the reference has them.

gaps.text: EMAIL cascade card seam is a hard-edged horizontal band, sharply cut top and bottom, rather than lines pinching into the seam; at full view it reads as a pasted stripe. The upper-left wavy figure of the reference is missing.

Panel veneer is soft and low-contrast next to the reference's crisp dark lines, and has a hard rectangular edge at the right of the lower figure; its crease is a strong straight diagonal where the reference's curves up.
Header labels (SECURITY LEVEL, LEVEL above T1-T4, LEVEL T1 at left) are dim tan where the reference's are bright amber; ghost copies of T2-T4 stronger than the reference's.
Panel body text slightly lighter and thinner than the reference's; panel fill slightly lighter (#FFC46E vs #F2B665).
C/D notes and card notes dim (MICRO ink) and squarer than the reference; EMAIL caption under the panel smaller and dimmer, no glow.

since_2026_11_13.text: Right EMAIL panel body thin, pale and letter-spaced, barely darker than the gold.
Selected EMAIL card: straight even vertical stripes, no book-match seam, no bevelled rim.
Right panel veneer nearly uniform, no curved figure or edge shading.
Header B note right-aligned against the badge and wider-spaced.
Fine-print blocks under the cards slightly bolder and squarer than the reference.

screens.question: The light text across all four screens is a pale cream where the reference prints saturated amber with a halo. Should light ink move toward the reference's amber (and a soft bloom be added), or is the paler cream a deliberate choice for legibility on the desktop?
